invariants.note: Single SWAP kernel remains unchanged; remediation is a runtime/coupler transaction seam.
No file, format, parsing, path or file-unit dependency introduced.
External groundwater state remains separate from SWAP parameters, forcing and physical state.
Only compact opaque transaction handles cross the seam; no full groundwater state is persisted per column.
Backend trial and reservation scratch remains service/worker owned.
Opaque handles preserve freedom for pooled, batched or SoA backend storage.

Prepare is reversible, abort leaves committed groundwater unchanged, and final prepared publication has no recoverable rejection path; this removes the normal-runtime half-commit gap identified before F-GC21.
Prepared publication retains the original committed revision and window; retry after abort returns to the same physical origin.
Generic finite [t0,t1] semantics remain unchanged.
No fixed duration or midnight boundary is introduced.
Transactional coupling publication is treated as first-class runtime functionality.
F-GC17 typed head/flux convention remains unchanged and locked.
No interface mass tolerance or compensating water adjustment is introduced; the remediation exists specifically to prevent asymmetric publication.
Interface sensitivity production and transport remain untouched.
Two-phase publication adds no full SWAP trajectory and no iterative coupling loop.
Prepared handles are lightweight and compatible with many logical columns and shared workers.
No 1:1 SWAP-column to groundwater-cell relationship is introduced.
Deep-vadose remains optional and outside SWAP.
Prepare/abort moves no physical water and introduces no hidden transition storage.
No soil-water solver implementation is assumed.
SWAP process physics is untouched and not duplicated.
No HeadCalc internals or solver arrays are referenced.
Transaction publication semantics remain separate from physical options and solver policy.
No retry ladder, fallback physics or unbounded work is introduced.
Reference mode remains unchanged.
Prepared, aborted and committed lifecycle states are explicit and diagnosable through typed handles/status before final publication.
Reservation state exists only for services opting into coupled two-phase publication.
External groundwater implementation and composition remain runtime/coupler-owned.
No MODFLOW, file-format, calendar or daily-run assumption is introduced.
The remediation and its atomicity rationale were explicitly audited before downstream composition.
